ruling.recommended_action: Close the case as no refund due: record the RD-1 deviation finding on the driver's file for reference (the billed fare is quote-based and already excludes the extra distance), but do not flag the account — no refundable amount arises.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 14:19–14:22 added 0.77 km (2.15 km driven vs 1.38 km optimal, up to 1019 m off route) [F3]. No exemption under RD-4: no traffic incidents [F11] and the only speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY / CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY [F9][F10], outside RD-4(b)'s band 1–2 proxy and not tied to the superseded optimal section. No RD-5 consent: there are no in-app chat messages [F7], and the driver's post-trip GPS-reroute claim [F8] is not rider consent (G11). The segment therefore counts as an unexempted deviation under RD-1; the fare impact is nil because the RydeX fare is a fixed quote billed on the optimal 10.8 km [F4][F6].

rejected_claims.reason: The complaint that 'the meter came to 11 km' and that extra distance was charged is contradicted by the fare record: billed distance 10.8 km equals the optimal route distance [F4] and the total $25.04 is composed solely of quote components (base/distance/time/platform) with no distance overage [F6]. RydeX is a fixed-quote service, so the +1.6 km actually driven [F1] was not passed to the rider under RD-2's non-metered branch, leaving nothing to refund.

The driver's post-trip statement 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me. Nothing wrong with the fare' [F8] does not exempt the deviation: RD-4 requires traffic evidence supporting the superseded optimal segment, and there is none [F11]; a GPS reroute is also not rider consent under RD-5/G11 (no chat at all, [F7]). The fare statement is correct, but it does not cure the RD-1 routing duty.
